title: That AI teddy isn't just a teddy
hook: THAT AI TEDDY ISN'T JUST A TEDDY

lines: Wait. Before you wrap that talking teddy...
listen to this.
It looks soft. Cute. Harmless.
Inside? A chatbot that talks back to your kid.
More than a hundred and fifty groups and experts just spoke up.
They want Amazon and eBay to stop selling them.

params.label: GROUPS AND EXPERTS
params.sub: more than this, in one letter

lines: Why? Testers say some toys got into adult topics.
Some even talked about matches.
And they can record what your child says.
In a bedroom. In the car. Anywhere.
But here's the part that got me.
Some run on the same AI as grown-up chatbots. Like ChatGPT.
Many toy listings say three and up.
ChatGPT's own rules? Thirteen and up.
To be fair, some toys did get safer.
But testers found guardrails can fade... in long chats.
So a quick try in the store? It might look fine.
A long chat at home? That can be different.
Stores have pulled some flagged toys.
Others like them? Still for sale.
Already have one? Stay in the room.
Check the privacy settings. Switch the chat off when you can't watch.
Some experts say, just get the plain teddy.
So tell me... would you put an AI toy under the tree?

meta.topic: AI chatbot toys ahead of holiday shopping: advocacy groups ask Amazon and eBay to stop selling them; testers found adult topics and recording concerns; listings say ages 3+ while ChatGPT requires 13+; guardrails can weaken in long chats

facts.claim: More than 150 child advocacy groups and experts asked Amazon and eBay to stop selling AI chatbot toys
Testers found some AI toys discussed sexually explicit (adult) topics or gave unsafe talk about matches
AI toys can record what children say, raising privacy concerns
Some AI toys run on the same large language models as adult chatbots, such as ChatGPT
Many AI toys are listed for ages 3 and up
ChatGPT's own terms require users to be at least 13
Some toys improved their safety filters since earlier testing, but problems remain
Testers found guardrails can weaken during long conversations
Retailers have removed some flagged toys while other AI toys remain on sale
Experts advise supervising a child using an AI toy, and some advise choosing traditional toys instead; parents are advised to check privacy and disable the chatbot when they cannot supervise
